text: With identity federated, security engineering turns to the combined fleet's hardening baseline — a real GPO and CIS-based program covering Windows, plus a Linux pass for servers that were never hardened at all.

The combined fleet is roughly 2,700 Windows endpoints — Castellan's original 2,400 plus Thornbury's 380 — and about forty Linux servers Thornbury's actuarial team runs for risk modeling, previously unmanaged under any formal hardening program. A scan finds exactly the gaps Chapter 4 predicts: stored LAN Manager hashes, LLMNR and SMBv1 still enabled, and zero Attack Surface Reduction rules configured anywhere on Thornbury's machines.

The fix is a new GPO, scoped through security filtering and OU targeting, never an edit to the Default Domain Policy. It disables LLMNR and SMBv1, blocks LAN Manager hash storage, enables Credential Guard to isolate LSA secrets from malware with local admin, and turns on the ASR rules Chapter 4 recommends against macro payloads and credential theft.

Thornbury's forty Linux servers get the same discipline, scaled to the platform: a scan against the CIS Benchmark for Ubuntu Server, sysctl kernel hardening from Chapter 5, and the entire remediation written as an Ansible playbook instead of applied by hand, so it's repeatable and reusable on the next server provisioned.

Neither baseline goes straight to enforcement. A 150-machine pilot group — Thornbury's whole Windows fleet plus Castellan's own helpdesk team — runs both for two weeks, ASR rules in audit mode and the playbook's riskier changes in a dry run. It catches a real actuarial cron job the new sysctl restrictions would have broken, and a finance team's legacy macro-enabled spreadsheet an ASR rule would have blocked outright.

Both findings become documented, owned, time-limited exceptions instead of either stalling the rollout or leaving a quiet hole in the baseline. With exceptions tracked, enforcement rolls out in waves. Next up: a governance gap from before the merger that this program's own access certification campaign is about to surface.
